name: Tomato Water BLT
desc: A Middle Child style BLT with salt-sweated heirloom tomatoes and arugula dressed in a vinaigrette made from their own juice.

source.title: Tomato Water BLT (Middle Child copycat)
source.evidence: Saved Instagram reel; caption and on-screen text captured in the owner's saved-recipes export

ingredients.raw: 2 large heirloom tomatoes (about 1 1/2 lb), sliced 1/2 in thick
2 tbsp tomato water (collected from the tomatoes)
1/4 tsp dried oregano or Italian herbs (optional)
Salt and black pepper, to taste

steps: Set a wire cooling rack over a rimmed baking sheet. Lay the tomato slices on the rack in one layer and salt them heavily on both sides.
Let the tomatoes sweat at room temperature for 2 hours or more. The tomato water collects in the pan below.
About 30 min before assembling, heat the oven to 400°F. Lay the bacon on a parchment-lined sheet pan and bake 18 to 25 min, until crisp. Drain on paper towels.
Pour the tomato water from the pan into a small bowl. Whisk 2 tbsp of it with the olive oil, sherry vinegar, herbs and pepper. Taste before adding any salt, since the tomato water is already salty.
Toss the arugula with enough vinaigrette to coat.
Spread the mayonnaise edge to edge on one side of each bread slice.
On 2 of the slices, layer the tomatoes, the dressed arugula and 5 slices of bacon each. Close with the remaining bread, cut in half and serve.
tips: Salting concentrates the tomato flavor, and the drained water becomes the dressing.
Middle Child serves theirs on rye. The mayo edge to edge is meant to protect the bread, though the tomato juice soaks through anyway.

references.title: Garden Salad with Tomato-Water Vinaigrette
references.usedFor: tomato water to oil to vinegar ratio, tasting before salting because the tomato water is salty
